name: Katti
description: Katti (meaning 'cut' or 'bundle' in some dialects) is a traditional Indian banking and gambling game of pure chance, closely related to Andar Bahar. Originating in South India (Karnataka and Tamil Nadu), the game involves betting on which of two piles ('Andar'/Inside or 'Bahar'/Outside) will first receive a card matching the rank of a central 'House' card. It is a staple of festival gambling and modern online casinos.

content.text: Katti (meaning 'cut' or 'bundle' in some dialects) is a traditional Indian banking and gambling game of pure chance, closely related to Andar Bahar. Originating in South India (Karnataka and Tamil Nadu), the game involves betting on which of two piles ('Andar'/Inside or 'Bahar'/Outside) will first receive a card matching the rank of a central 'House' card. It is a staple of festival gambling and modern online casinos.

Believed to have originated in Bengaluru (Bangalore). In Tamil, it is often called 'Mangatha' or 'Ullae Veliyae' (Inside Outside). The game reflects the communal nature of Indian betting, where speed and simplicity are prioritized.
One dealer (Bank) and theoretically unlimited players.
Standard 52-card deck. Shuffled thoroughly and cut.

Bank shuffles and deals one card face-up (House card), then two piles (Andar and Bahar) one card each.
